terms.definition: Automated external defibrillator: a device that analyzes the heart rhythm and gives a shock only when its algorithm identifies a shockable rhythm.
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: chest compressions, with rescue breaths when trained and willing, used when a person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.
The trained call handler in a control centre who gathers information, sends suitable help, and may coach immediate actions.
A sign or situation that overrides ordinary self-care and changes the route to urgent or emergency help.
A stable side-lying position used for an unresponsive person who is breathing normally when movement is not prevented by major trauma.
Prioritizing action by urgency and likely harm; in this guide it is a lay routing aid, not a clinical diagnosis.
Processing signals from inside the body, including sensing, attention, interpretation, prediction, and regulation.
Keeping an essential function operating through a named owner, backup, review time, and escalation route.
The person who adapts, prints, places, checks, and maintains a local copy of the guide.
Any person using the guide in the moment; the reader is never assumed to be the deployer.
A stable typed address such as [BEG:C:S:004]. The ID stays stable even when page numbers or surrounding sections move.
The boundary of what a source, study, protocol, or model can honestly establish.
An observation such as breathing, pulse, temperature, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, or glucose that may help a handoff but cannot by itself clear a red flag.
